title: Maureen, back again

greeting.text: The bell. The quilted vest. A thermos this time, and the paper plate again.
Only me, love. Road's still shut, so I thought: those two up at the roadhouse. Did you eat the scone?
A fresh one goes down where last night's was. She looks at your face while you look at it. She is counting something.

annoyed: Twice now you've looked me over like a parcel, dear.

notes.wrist: The kiss-clasp purse. The same thin skin, the same blue map under it.
notes.reflection: A small bent back and a grey bun. It moves when she moves.
notes.shadow: One shadow, soft, tucked under her. The radio would approve.

topics.answer: Quiet. Too quiet. Something walked round the van at about three. I said 'Ken?' before I could stop myself. It stopped walking.

topics.ask: Stay a while. It's good to see a face twice.
topics.answer: Now that is the nicest thing I've heard since Tarrow.
topics.note: Wren sets a glass down harder than a glass needs.

topics.ask: Maureen. Do I look the same as last night?
topics.answer: ...What a question. Yes. Exactly the same. Not a hair different. Isn't that funny? Most people look worse the second night.

topics.ask: You shouldn't keep coming up here.
topics.answer: No. I don't suppose I should. But somebody ought to check on you, and I don't think anybody is.

wren.arrive: Her again. She's brought a thermos. She's planning to stay.
wren.adviceLine: She keeps looking at you, Sam. Counting things. Send her away for good this time. For me.

after.serve: You like her more than me. Say it. ...No. Don't.
after.turnAway: Thank you. That's twice you've picked me. I'm keeping count.
after.shelter: She's on the cot again. She asked me how long I've known you. I said: all my life.

serve.text: Park under the canopy lights tonight. Lock the van.

turnAway.text: Don't come back up here, Maureen. Please.
...Is that you asking, love, or the other one?

shelter.text: Stay in the back tonight. It isn't safe out there.
With that one holding the key? ...Well. I've slept in worse.

walkout.text: I'll not come a third time. I know when I'm not wanted, and I know when I'm being measured.

report.serve: The woman in the campervan at Corrigan's is well, and says the night attendant has not touched a thing she's baked.
report.turnAway: A campervan left the Corrigan's lay-by at speed at about eleven. It has not been seen at either roadblock.
report.walkout: A campervan left the Corrigan's lay-by at speed at about eleven. It has not been seen at either roadblock.
report.shelter: A traveller sheltered again at Corrigan's. She tells us somebody knocked all night, from inside the walls.
report.missed: The campervan in Corrigan's lay-by has its curtains drawn. Nobody has answered the door.
